document.title: Is There an Upper Limit to Computer Processing Speed? A Physical Compute-Envelope Contract for Defensible Throughput Claims

source_controls.discovery_method: OpenAlex and AnySearch Academic were queried in parallel and duplicate DOI records were cross-validated.

browser_metadata_check.verified_record: Deffner and Campbell, Quantum speed limits: from Heisenberg's uncertainty principle to optimal quantum control, Journal of Physics A, 2017

source_controls.human_review_required: Publisher or full-text applicability review is still required for each cited source before any real research execution or submission.

claim_boundary.supported_conclusion: Useful accepted computation is limited by a workload- and resource-bounded physical envelope rather than a single technology-independent scalar speed ceiling.
not_claimed: a universal tight numerical upper bound for every computer and workload
executed hardware, simulation, benchmark, or measurement results
general-purpose quantum superiority from a sampling demonstration
